# Coverly ROMs

> Free desktop app (AGPL-3.0-only) for Windows, macOS and Linux that audits a ROM library, such as a handheld's SD card, shows which games lack cover, screenshot or title-screen art, and fills them in bulk from libretro-thumbnails (no account) or SteamGridDB (your own key). A dry run comes first, existing art is never overwritten unless you ask (and then it is backed up), and the last job can be undone. Around the covers it sorts downloads into 131 systems (archives, disc games and games that are a folder included) and sets duplicates aside, both with a dry run and undo. It ships with a command line, `coverly`. No account, no telemetry. Made by Miguel Esparza (MAECLY).

Builds carry no Apple or Microsoft code-signing certificate, so macOS Gatekeeper ("Open Anyway") and Windows SmartScreen ("More info", then "Run anyway") warn the first time. Downloads can be checked against SHA256SUMS.

## What it does today

- Audit: scans a library (systems, ROMs including multi-file .cue/.bin, .m3u, .gdi and folder games) and reports, per media type (cover, screenshot, title screen), what is present or missing. Read-only. Exports CSV or JSON.
- Layout profiles, detected automatically: Anbernic stock, GarlicOS, Onion OS, MinUI / NextUI (cover); muOS (cover, screenshot); ES-DE, RetroArch (cover, screenshot, title); Batocera / Knulli / EmulationStation (cover, screenshot, title, plus gamelist.xml merging with undo). Custom profiles with your own path templates and a live preview.
- 131 known systems with the folder aliases each firmware uses.
- Identification: CRC32, MD5 and SHA1 against libretro-database, then the file name; arcade short names through MAME and FBNeo DATs. Method selectable: hash-then-name, hash-only, name-only. .7z archives are identified by name only.
- Sources: libretro-thumbnails (default, no account); SteamGridDB (optional, your own API key, kept in the OS keychain).
- Choosing the image: by the ROM's region (default order rom, world, usa, europe, japan), by source priority, or by popularity (SteamGridDB votes, then agreement between sources). Each choice says why.
- Safety: dry run by default; only missing art by default; existing art replaced only if you choose overwrite-with-backup; nothing written outside the library folder; atomic writes; backups and job journals in the app data folder, not on the card; undo of the last job; uncertain matches go to a keyboard-driven review queue; jobs pause, resume and cancel; one failing item never stops a job; offline or rate-limited jobs pause; file names safe for FAT/exFAT; macOS ._ files ignored.
- Organise: sorts a folder of loose ROMs into system folders for any layout profile, moving or copying, never overwriting, with a dry run, resume and undo (`coverly organize`). Archives are recognised by their contents: zip, 7z, tar, gzip, bzip2, xz, zstd, lz4 and single compressed ROMs; RAR through a program already installed (unrar, 7-Zip or bsdtar). Disc games inside archives are identified from the disc (PlayStation, Sega Saturn, Dreamcast, Sega CD, PC Engine CD, Neo Geo CD) and extracted on apply, each file verified by size and CRC.
- Duplicates: finds the same game stored more than once in a system by its contents, never its name (exact copies, the same disc in another format, and other versions only with "One ROM per game"). One copy stays, picked by rules you can reorder; the others are set aside in `_Duplicados/` inside the library, with their saves, states and art, or sent to the Trash. Copies with different saves are never touched. Dry run first, resume and undo; nothing is deleted (`coverly dedupe`, dry run unless --apply).
- App: library browser (folders, systems, date, all) with six views on Cmd/Ctrl+1-6 (Covers, Details, Columns, Gallery, Art slots, Shelves), an icon beside every system name, filters and search, a detail panel per game (change, search, from file, remove), fill wizard, connected drives on the start screen, English and Spanish, light/dark/system themes.
- CLI: coverly audit, fill (dry run unless --apply; --auto-only skips review items), organize, dedupe, profiles, systems, undo, update.
- Privacy: no telemetry. Network requests only to the art sources and the optional update check. Images are decoded and re-encoded, which strips metadata.
- Updates: in-app, from GitHub Releases, verified with minisign; stable and beta channels; never restarts during a job.

## Next version (already in the code, not in a published release yet)

- 131 systems, up from 54: retro consoles, handhelds, computers, arcade boards, ports and engines, fantasy consoles, GameCube, Wii, Wii U, 3DS, Switch, PS Vita, PS3, PS4, PS5, Xbox, Xbox 360, Xbox One and Xbox Series (catalogued only).
- Current consoles recognised without keys, from what is stored in the clear; anything unreadable is labelled "Encrypted". Coverly never reads, asks for, downloads or ships console keys, and leaves key and licence files untouched.
- Optional Switch name catalogue from blawar/titledb (MIT), off by default.
- Covers: the icon a game carries (PS3, PS Vita, Wii U, 3DS, Xbox 360) when no source has one; PS4, PS5, Xbox One and Xbox Series try it first. RetroArch thumbnails of titles with characters such as & or : are named the way RetroArch looks for them.
- Organise: games that are a folder move as one item, from inside zip and 7z archives too; loose multi-disc games are grouped with an .m3u; each item of 10 GB or more asks first ("Yes / Yes to all / No"), and `coverly organize --skip-large` leaves them in place.
- Duplicates by title ID and version, and by the same folder; updates and DLC are listed under their game.
- Settings: a Credits tab listing 62 sources, databases and libraries with their licences; Organise and Duplicates in their own tabs with search.
- Downloads named by system and chip: separate Apple silicon and Intel Mac builds, and Windows ARM64.
- CLI: `coverly catalog switch status|update|remove`.

## Not supported

- ScreenScraper (planned; not available in public builds).
- TheGamesDB; mixed/composite images, videos, marquees, wheels.
- Editing gamelist metadata, renaming or verifying ROMs.
- Running on the handheld itself.
- It bundles no ROMs, BIOS files or game art. Game art belongs to its owners.
- Not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Sony, Microsoft, Sega or any other maker; system names are their owners' trademarks, used only to say what it works with. The system icons on the site are adapted from RetroArch Assets (XMB Monochrome theme), (c) libretro contributors, CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
- Not yet tested on real handhelds; the maximum image sizes some firmware accepts are not confirmed.
